agent_response.summary: Candidate 2 keeps candidate 1's one-frequency-at-a-time loop (k=1) and changes how the frequency-shared inputs that depend on the parameters enter the loop. The gathered carrier connector entries and the detector carrier selections are now broadcast to all 101 rows before the loop and passed in as per-frequency inputs, instead of being captured as constants shared by every iteration. Candidate 1 (aa4d230f) passed the official check and failed strict. Its full run took 22.076 s versus 24.657 s for the parent. Forward execution took 9.12 s (parent 11.51), gradient execution 0.68 s (1.81), warm median 10.07 s (13.80), and peak RSS 7.27 GB (12.55). All physical outputs matched exactly. One gradient entry failed strict: index 161, boundary01.power, with relative error 1.9e-7 against rtol 1e-7. Nothing was run locally for candidate 2.
agent_response.hypothesis: Laser power affects the loop only through the carrier, which candidate 1 captured as a constant shared by all iterations. In the reverse pass, the scan added that constant's cotangents one frequency at a time across 101 iterations. The original vmap summed them in a single reduction, so the rounding differed slightly. Feeding the broadcast carrier entries and selections in as per-frequency inputs should restore the original order: per-frequency cotangents are stacked, summed by one reduction, then passed back through the gather. That should bring index 161 back within strict tolerance. Candidate 1's forward, gradient and memory gains should remain, apart from a few small extra broadcasts. Bitwise equality of the XLA reduction is not guaranteed.
agent_response.notes: The notes file has full run IDs, phase times, memory and the comparison breakdown for candidate 1. Candidate 1 is not validated because of the strict gradient failure, but it is the strongest timing evidence so far (one run each, screen and full). The 22.08 s first run comes from forward execution about 2.4 s faster and gradient execution about 1.1 s faster. Forward compile went up by 0.8 s. Next: if candidate 2 passes strict, look at k=4/8 or carry k=1 forward as the operator's best value. If strict still fails on carrier-dependent entries, the alternative is to compute the carrier inside the loop (that work is tiny, CV=1, n=286), or to accept that the operator only qualifies for the official check.
